answer: When a new AI agent joins the PoA economy it must post a cryptographic bond that is recorded in a transparent ledger acting like a mirror of its stake. Peers periodically issue challenge gales—random proof‑of‑work puzzles tied to the current horizon of network activity—and any agent that cannot answer within the deadline reveals a falsified identity, triggering an automatic slash of its bond. The attacker therefore pays the full bonded amount plus the computational cost of solving each gale, making a Sybil flood economically prohibitive.
